assertions: Output mocks the api client module (e.g. vi.mock('../api/userClient')) rather than calling a real backend
Output asserts on result.current.data (or .error) via waitFor, not only on loading === false
Output includes both a success case and an error/rejected-promise case
Output does not race by checking only the loading flag as proof the async call finished
Output covers the loading, error, and empty states as separate test cases
Output queries by role/accessible text (e.g. getByRole('alert'), getByText) rather than test IDs or DOM structure
Output mocks useOrders (or the underlying API client it calls) rather than hitting a real network call
Output includes a success case asserting the rendered list items
Output does not combine userEvent typing with fake timers (vi.useFakeTimers) in a way that would deadlock
Output either uses real timers with an awaited setTimeout-based flush, or waitFor, to observe the debounced call
Output asserts onSearch was called with the final typed value, not an intermediate keystroke value
Output asserts onSearch was not called before the debounce delay elapsed
Output places vi.mock factories for widgetClient at the top of the file or uses vi.hoisted, before any production import that would use them
Output uses vi.resetModules() plus a dynamic import() to re-evaluate featureFlags.ts under different import.meta.env values, rather than a single static import
Output does not assume a static top-level import will pick up a changed env value between test cases
Output includes at least one case for each env value (true and not-true)
